joinSession.intro: This calculator measures your individual carbon footprint — not your family's or your shared household's.
joinSession.privacyNote: Your age, gender and carbon footprint are collected anonymously for the workshop results. They aren't linked to any name or shared with third parties.

errors.notStarted: The workshop hasn't started yet. Wait for the facilitator.

intro.title: Before you start
intro.p1: This is an individual questionnaire! Answer the questions for yourself, not on behalf of your household. Of course, some things are shared (your home with your family, the car with the people you share journeys with, etc.). That's taken into account when calculating your footprint, so don't worry.
intro.p2: The questions are about your personal life, not your work activity.

home.heroSub: Transport, food, energy at home… it all adds up. In 5 minutes you'll know exactly how much CO₂e your life generates — and how you compare with your team.
home.joinDesc: Enter the code your facilitator gave you to calculate your footprint.

errors.format: The code must be in the format DROP-0000

stats.spainAvg: Average CO₂e per person per year in Ireland
stats.double: Twice what the planet can absorb

steps.s1Text: The facilitator shares a code. Join from your phone, no sign-up or install.
steps.s2Text: Answer questions about transport, energy, food and more.
steps.s3Text: Compare with your team and the Irish average in real time.

carKm.text: How many km do you drive a year?
carKm.info: Count the km you drive to work, on trips and on holiday. If you regularly share a car, count the total km.

options.km_d: I use it a lot — over 20,000 km/year
options.km_e: I don't have a car or don't use it

flights.text: How many flights do you take a year?
flights.info: Count a return flight as one. Enter 0 if you don't fly.

train.text: How much do you use the train?

options.3b: Quite a bit for holidays and trips (1,000–5,000 km)

moto.text: Do you have a petrol motorbike or scooter?

options.4c: I use it for everything (over 1,000 km/year)

urbanMobility.text: How do you usually get around the city?
urbanMobility.info: Short city journeys are where there's the most room to improve.

telework.text: Can you work from home? How often do you?
telework.info: Working from home cuts commuting and, with it, the emissions linked to transport

options.never: Never, I go to the office every day

homeType.text: What type of home do you live in?
homeType.info: Home size directly affects heating and cooling use.

options.25c: Large house or detached home (over 180 m²)

heating.text: What heating system do you have?
heating.info: This question covers heating, hot water and cooking. Emission factor adapted to the Spanish grid.

renewable.text: Do you have solar panels or a 100% renewable energy tariff?
renewable.info: Renewable energy cuts your electricity footprint and your reliance on imported fuels.

options.a: Yes, I have solar panels at home
options.b: I have a certified 100% renewable electricity tariff
options.c: No, I use standard grid electricity

hasAC.info: If you have fans but no air conditioning, tick No.

homeHabits.text: Do you do any of these at home? (tick all that apply)
homeHabits.info: Small actions that cut your home's energy use.

options.closeWindows: I close the windows when I turn on the heating.
options.thermostat19: I keep the heating at 19–20°C (no higher)
options.ecoPrograms: I use the eco programmes on my washing machine and dishwasher
options.none: I don't do any of these

vacationNights.text: When you go on holiday, where do you stay?
vacationNights.info: Think of a typical year. You can leave the ones you don't use at 0.

breakfastDays.text: What do you usually have for breakfast during the week?
breakfastDays.info: Spread your 7 days across the breakfast types. If you also snack mid-morning, turn on the option.

hotDrinksCount.text: How many hot drinks do you have a day?
hotDrinksCount.info: Enter how many of each type you have on average per day.

alcohol.text: How much do you drink in a normal week (including the weekend)?
alcohol.info: No judgement — it all adds to your footprint. Think of a typical week including the weekend. Leave what you don't drink at 0.

lunchDays.text: What do you usually have for lunch in a typical week?
lunchDays.info: Spread your 7 weekly meals across the types. Both at home and eating out.

dinnerDays.text: What do you usually have for dinner in a typical week?
dinnerDays.info: Spread your 7 weekly dinners across the types.

bottledWater.info: If you mainly drink tap water, tick no. Tap water is safe to drink in most places.

options.13a: Yes, we buy bottled water at home

foodHabits.text: Do you usually do any of these? (tick all that apply)
foodHabits.info: Small actions that cut your food footprint.

options.none: I don't do any of these

deliveryPerWeek.text: How many food deliveries do you order a week?
deliveryPerWeek.info: Each order adds about 3 kgCO₂e (last-mile transport + packaging).

clothes.text: How many new clothes do you buy a year? (garments and shoes included)
clothes.info: Jumpers, trousers, coats, shoes... Count everything that's new. Second-hand clothes have an almost zero footprint.

electronics.text: What new devices have you bought in the last year? (tick all)
electronics.info: If you bought it 1–2 years ago you can count it. If it was over 3 years ago, don't.

appliances.text: Which appliances under 5 years old do you have at home? (tick all)
appliances.info: Making appliances has a big footprint. If they're over 5 years old, don't count them.

pets.info: Pet food (especially for dogs and cats) has a real carbon footprint — mainly from the meat in their food.

hygiene.text: How many hygiene and cleaning products do you buy a month?
hygiene.info: Shampoo, shower gel, make-up, creams, detergents, household cleaning products...

sports.text: What sports do you usually do?
sports.info: Tick all that you do. The footprint includes facilities, travel and gear.

options.racket: Racket or ball sports (tennis, football, padel...)

videoCalls.text: How often do you make video calls? (Zoom, Teams, Meet...)

options.vc_lots: A lot, I love a video call (over 5 h/week)

streaming.text: How often do you watch streaming? (Netflix, YouTube, HBO...)

socialMedia.text: How often do you use social media? (Instagram, TikTok, X...)

aiUsage.text: How much do you use AI tools a day? (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot...)
aiUsage.info: A query to a large AI model uses about 10× more energy than a Google search.

rankings.fewDataWarning: With little data, the distribution may not be representative.

t01.title: I take the train instead of flying for a weekend getaway.

t02.title: I swap an island holiday for Cantabria, and the plane for the car, travelling at least two of us.
t02.description: I choose a domestic destination and share the journey.

t03.title: I take the bus instead of the car for my daily journeys.
t03.description: An urban bus emits up to 6× less CO₂e per passenger.

t04.title: I cycle instead of driving for my daily journeys.

t05.title: I take the train instead of the car for my daily journeys.
t05.description: Commuter trains emit up to 10× less than the car.

t06.title: I choose a short-haul flight instead of a transoceanic one for my holidays (for example, a European city instead of New York).
t06.description: I go to Lisbon instead of New York.

t07.title: I share a car with at least two other people for a weekend trip.

v01.title: I replace my fossil fuel heating with a heat pump (and my energy bills can go down too).
v01.description: It also lowers my energy bill.

v02.title: I replace my light bulbs with energy-efficient LED bulbs.
v02.description: LEDs use up to 80% less energy.

v03.title: I keep the temperature at home at 19.5°C in winter.
v03.description: Each degree lower saves 7% on heating.

v04.title: I close windows when the heating is on

v05.title: I use the eco programmes on my appliances.
v05.description: It saves hot water and electricity.

v06.title: I hang my clothes out to dry instead of using the tumble dryer.
v06.description: The tumble dryer is one of the most power-hungry appliances.

v07.title: I unplug electronic devices when not in use.
v07.description: Standby mode can account for up to 10% of the bill.

a01.title: I stop eating meat.
a01.description: One of the highest-impact individual actions.

a02.title: I make compost at home.
a02.description: It cuts the methane from organic waste in landfill.

a03.title: I replace red meat with white meat (at least once per week).

a04.title: I limit beef to 1 meal a week.
a04.description: I replace the rest with vegetables, fruit and grains.

a05.title: I buy in bulk.
a05.description: It cuts packaging and food waste.

a06.title: I eat seasonal and local food.

a07.title: I take part in initiatives like "Meatless Monday"
a07.description: One meat-free day a week makes a difference.

a08.title: I have just 1 coffee a day.
a08.description: Coffee has a significant water and carbon footprint.

a09.title: I replace one cup of coffee with tea each day.
a09.description: Tea emits up to 4× less CO₂e than coffee.

a10.title: I stop drinking water from plastic bottles (I use a reusable bottle).
a10.description: It cuts out making and shipping plastic.

c01.title: I buy repaired appliances.
c01.description: I contribute to the circular economy.

c02.title: I buy fewer clothes, but of better quality.
c02.description: Fast fashion causes 10% of global emissions.

c03.title: I buy or swap second-hand items.
c03.description: Extending a product's life cuts its footprint.

c04.title: I buy second-hand clothes.
c04.description: Each reused garment saves water, energy and emissions.

c05.title: I repair my broken appliances.
c05.description: Extending its life by 2 years halves its footprint.

c06.title: I choose more sustainable sports, like running instead of golf.
c06.description: Golf needs large areas of land and water.

c07.title: I choose eco-friendly and biodegradable cleaning products.
c07.description: Fewer chemicals, less energy in production.

c08.title: I give my smartphone a second chance.
c08.description: Manufacturing is 80% of a phone's footprint.

c09.title: I quit smoking.
c09.description: As well as the health benefits, it cuts waste and emissions.

d01.title: I cancel digital subscriptions I don't use
d01.description: Every active cloud service uses energy even when you don't.

d02.title: I stream in basic quality instead of HD when I don't need it, reducing data use by 80%.

d03.title: I stream music as audio instead of video (Spotify vs YouTube).
d03.description: Audio uses one-tenth as much as video.

d04.title: I use AI only when I need it.
d04.description: An AI query uses 10 times more energy than a search engine.

d05.title: I delete unused cloud content: photos, files and emails.
d05.description: Servers never rest: less data, less energy.
